title_line: Modern Data Architecture: Lake, Warehouse, Lakehouse, Mesh

concepts.name: Data Warehouse
concepts.text: Structured, cleaned and modeled data for SQL analytics and BI; strong at complex joins and many concurrent users.

concepts.name: Data Lake
concepts.text: Data of any format and size in raw form; cheap, durable storage with decoupled compute and reprocessing from raw.

concepts.name: Lakehouse
concepts.text: Lake storage plus warehouse features: ACID, updates/deletes, schema evolution, time travel.

concepts.name: Data Mesh
concepts.text: Domain teams publish data products; a central team runs the platform and global governance.
concepts.tag: Amazon SageMaker Catalog + AWS Lake Formation

items.label: Raw / Bronze
items.text: Immutable copies of source data in the original format; keep them so you can replay.

items.label: Cleansed / Silver
items.text: Deduplicated, typed and validated; converted to Parquet / Iceberg.

items.label: Curated / Gold
items.text: Business-level aggregates, conformed dimensions and data products.

nodes.label: Sales domain account: S3 + Glue Catalog

table.heading: Data Sharing Patterns
rows: One account holds all data; Lake Formation grants to consumers
Producers own data; central catalog; LF grants via AWS RAM
AWS Data Exchange (files, APIs, Redshift datashares, S3 access)
store all raw data cheaply, any format, reprocess later
S3 data lake + Glue Data Catalog
complex SQL, BI dashboards, consistent performance at high concurrency
updates/deletes and time travel on lake data
Apache Iceberg tables or S3 Tables
domains own their data, central discovery and approval
share live Redshift data with another account, no copies

tips: "No copies / no data movement" points to data sharing, Spectrum, federated query or Lake Formation grants, not exports.
Upserts or GDPR deletes on S3 data need Iceberg (or Hudi/Delta), not rewriting partitions by hand.
Lake Formation stores no data: it governs access to S3 data and catalog resources.
Don't put raw, unstructured or rarely queried data in the warehouse: costly and inflexible.
